content.text: The text surveys Roman, Sassanian, Byzantine, Armenian, Russian, Lombard, Romanesque, and Italian Gothic architecture. It emphasizes inward-looking Roman houses, atria, courtyards, painted decoration, bridges, aqueducts, vaults, domes, and engineering. Sassanian palaces developed tunnel-vaulted halls, pendentive domes, and Persian adaptations of Roman forms. Constantine transferred the imperial government to Byzantium; Justinian later created Hagia Sophia, the high point of Byzantine architecture. Byzantine basilicas evolved from Roman models, while Armenian and Russian churches transmitted eastern forms northward. Western styles developed through basilican, Lombard, Romanesque, and Gothic experimentation, especially vaulting, towers, pointed arches, and polychrome decoration. Italy blended Roman, Byzantine, Lombard, and Gothic influences, producing celebrated monuments at Ravenna, Venice, Pisa, Florence, Siena, Milan, and elsewhere.
